product_name: Foldable Corrugated-Box Corner Protector & Edge Guard Set (ECT-Rated)

target_buyer.description: Someone shipping or moving boxes (reseller, small mover, or frequent shipper) whose boxes keep arriving with crushed corners despite using foam padding
target_buyer.context: My boxes still crush at the corners in the truck even with foam padding on them.

must_keep: ECT-32 rated corrugate (a stated, printed Edge Crush Test value) with HDPE reinforcement caps
must_avoid: a supplier substituting a lower ECT-grade linerboard than specified, so the printed rating overstates real crush resistance and corners fail on the same routes

user_hypotheses: A shipper whose foam-padded boxes still crush at the corners will buy a stated-crush-rating corner/edge protector set specifically because it lets them match protector strength to box weight instead of guessing at foam density
assumptions: Category tags from the sourcing brief: Storage, moving, packing & shipping; PUBLISHED-SPEC; NEW listing; FRAGILE MARGIN; LOW BARRIER to entry

Prior sourcing estimate (unverified against live fees, to be checked by scout/genius): FOB $1.70/unit, freight+drayage $0.30, duty 33% blended on FOB $0.56, prep/poly bag/FNSKU $0.25, landed cost $2.81; referral fee 15% $2.10, FBA fulfilment (8oz tier) $3.38, monthly storage (modeled) $0.04, Amazon fees $5.52; returns reserve 1.6% $0.22, PPC 9.0% TACoS $1.26, ads+returns $1.48; ASP $13.99, net profit $4.18, margin 29.9%
Sourcing logistics from the brief: tooling $300, MOQ 1,500 units, 2 parts, 3 weeks to first article; packed weight 8oz (small standard tier), packed volume (modeled) 90 cu in
Closest incumbent named in the brief: plain foam corner protectors sold for furniture shipping, ~$8-10, no stated crush rating

Differentiator proposed in the brief: die-cut from board rated to a stated Edge Crush Test (ECT-32) value, printed on the pack, so a shipper can match protector strength to box weight instead of guessing at foam density
Main sourcing risk flagged in the brief: a cheap supplier drops to a lower ECT-grade linerboard to cut cost, so the printed rating overstates real crush resistance and corners fail on the same routes
Regulatory position per the brief: none — ECT is an industry test spec, not a government certification; note on packaging as a manufacturer spec, not a regulatory claim
Back-end/repeat-purchase idea from the brief: bulk refill packs for repeat movers/shippers
In the box per the brief: 8 corner protectors + 4 edge guards, ECT-32 rated corrugate with HDPE reinforcement caps
